items.q: What is the Ultimate Assistant allowed to do?
items.a: Only **route** the user's query to the correct tool. The prompt says it should **never write emails or event summaries** — specialists handle the work.

items.q: Why four specialist agents instead of one mega-agent?
items.a: **Email, Calendar, Contact, and Content Creator** each get a **short prompt** and scoped tools. That scales better than one agent loaded with every tool and a huge system prompt.

Use **Call n8n Workflow as Tool**. Sub-workflows start with **Execute Workflow Trigger**; the last node returns `response`. Tool names in **camelCase** (`emailAgent`, `calendarAgent`) must match the system prompt.

items.q: How does the model fill Gmail and Calendar fields?
items.a: **$fromAI** lets the model fill tool params (to, subject, body, message ID) from natural language — no hand-written parsing. Tavily HTTP search uses the same idea with `{{searchTerm}}` placeholders.

items.q: Why do reply/label/delete actions need a prior "get"?
items.a: It's an **ID-chaining** pattern: fetch emails, labels, or events first, then pass those IDs into the action tool for reply, label, mark-unread, delete, or update.

items.q: What must happen before drafting email or inviting attendees?
items.a: The orchestrator must call the **Contact Agent** first and pass the **resolved email** into the downstream email or calendar query.
Sub-workflows use **On Error: Continue (Error Output)** → a `try again` branch so the orchestrator can retry with a new query instead of dying mid-run.

items.q: How do voice and text share one agent input?
items.a: A **Switch** routes voice → transcription or text → both map to `json.text`, so one agent input field serves both. Memory buffer keeps context like "push it back an hour."
**GPT-4o** for the orchestrator and most sub-agents; **Claude 3.5 Sonnet** for the Content Creator (HTML blog structure). Free JSON templates ship via the AI Automation Society Skool resources.
